<td valign="top" style="width:3.85%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#8226;</font></p></td>
<td valign="top">
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;color:#231F20;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">meaningful<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>commercial<font style="letter-spacing:0.15pt;"> </font>potential.</p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-right:2.99%;text-indent:5.38%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We have built<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>a compelling<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>portfolio<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>of gene therapy<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>product<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>candidates<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>and intend<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>to further<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>expand our portfolio<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>over<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>time.<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>Set forth<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>below is<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>a table<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>summarizing<font style="letter-spacing:0.15pt;"> </font>our development<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>programs.</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:13pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.38%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><img src="gg0d5mct2jc0000001.jpg" title="" alt="" style="width:546px;height:309px;"></p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.38%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">AT132.<font style="font-weight:normal;"> XLMTM is characterized by extreme muscle weakness, respiratory failure, and early death with an estimated 50% mortality rate in the first 18 months of life.&nbsp;&nbsp;The disease is the result of mutations in the </font><font style="font-style:italic;font-weight:normal;">MTM1</font><font style="font-weight:normal;"> gene that affect the production of myotubularin, an enzyme required for normal development and function of skeletal muscle.&nbsp;&nbsp;The incidence of XLMTM is estimated to be one in 40,000 to one in 50,000 male births.&nbsp;&nbsp;Currently, only supportive treatment options are available, such as ventilator use to aid breathing, wheelchair use to aid mobility, or&nbsp;&nbsp;feeding tube use to aid nutrition.</font></p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.38%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We are developing AT132, an AAV8 vector containing a functional copy of the <font style="font-style:italic;">MTM1</font> gene, for the treatment of XLMTM.&nbsp;&nbsp;We believe AT132 may provide patients with significantly improved outcomes based on the ability of AAV8 to transduce skeletal muscle.&nbsp;&nbsp;Over the course of 2018, Audentes reported promising safety, efficacy, and muscle biopsy data from ASPIRO, a multicenter, ascending dose Phase 1/2 clinical study designed to evaluate the safety and efficacy of AT132 in approximately 12 XLMTM patients less than five years of age.&nbsp;&nbsp;The<font style="color:#000000;"> latest </font><font style="color:#231F20;">ASPIRO data set (presented in October 2018) included safety and efficacy results ranging from 4 to 48 weeks for eight patients enrolled in the trial, including seven patients enrolled in Cohort 1 (1x10<sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">14</sup> vg/kg; six treated and one untreated control) and the sentinel patient in Cohort 2 (3x10<sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">14</sup> vg/kg), as well as week 24 muscle biopsy data for the first four treated patients.&nbsp;&nbsp;Subsequent to the October 2018 data set, we have completed initial enrollment of Cohort 2, and announced plans to further expand Cohort 2 with an additional three to five patients.</font></p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.38%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU6"></a>In the fourth quarter of 2018, we completed productive initial interactions with the FDA, under the RMAT designation, and EMA, under the PRIME designation, to discuss development plans and the potential registration pathways for AT132. Feedback from the agencies was largely aligned, and we agreed that selection of the optimal dose is a key next step in the development of AT132<font style="color:#000000;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;Optimal dose selection is expected to occur in the second </font></p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">3</p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><font style="color:#000000;">quarter of 2019</font><font style="color:#000000;">, after the evaluation of the six-month biopsy results from the first three patients dosed in Cohort 2</font><font style="color:#000000;"> </font><font style="color:#000000;">of ASPIRO</font><font style="color:#000000;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;Subsequent to the determination of the optimal dose, </font><font style="color:#000000;">we plan</font><font style="color:#000000;"> to provide an updated data package</font><font style="color:#000000;"> to </font><font style="color:#000000;">the </font><font style="color:#000000;">FDA </font><font style="color:#000000;">and EMA </font><font style="color:#000000;">to facilitate </font><font style="color:#000000;">final</font><font style="color:#000000;"> agreement on </font><font style="color:#000000;">license registration pathways</font><font style="color:#000000;">.&nbsp;&nbsp;</font><font style="color:#000000;">We</font><font style="color:#000000;"> also received preliminary feedback on </font><font style="color:#000000;">our</font><font style="color:#000000;"> </font><font style="color:#000000;">Chemistry Manufacturing and Controls, or </font><font style="color:#000000;">CMC</font><font style="color:#000000;">,</font><font style="color:#000000;"> characterization and validation plans and </font><font style="color:#000000;">plan to</font><font style="color:#000000;"> submit the requested information to the </font><font style="color:#000000;">respective trial applications </font><font style="color:#000000;">on a continuing basis</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">.</font></p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.38%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We have also initiated early commercialization and BLA readiness activities, including validation efforts at our in-house cGMP manufacturing facility.&nbsp;&nbsp;AT132 has been granted RMAT, Rare Pediatric Disease, Fast Track, and Orphan Drug designations by the FDA, and PRIME and Orphan Drug designations by the EMA.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.38%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">AT845.<font style="font-weight:normal;"> Pompe disease is a serious, progressive genetic disease characterized by severe muscle weakness, respiratory failure leading to ventilator dependence and, in infants, increased cardiac mass and heart failure.&nbsp;&nbsp;In untreated infants, the disease is often fatal due to cardio-respiratory failure within the first year of life, and in adults the disease is progressive and life-limiting with significant ventilator dependence and wheelchair use.&nbsp;&nbsp;Pompe disease is caused by mutations in the gene encoding the lysosomal enzyme alpha-glucosidase, or GAA, which results in a deficiency of GAA protein and leads to an intracellular accumulation of glycogen.&nbsp;&nbsp;The incidence of Pompe disease is approximately one in 40,000 births.&nbsp;&nbsp;The only approved treatment for Pompe disease is enzyme replacement therapy, or ERT, which is a chronic treatment delivered in bi-weekly intravenous infusions. Despite the availability of ERT, significant medical need still persists, which is primarily due to the inability of ERT to penetrate key tissues affected by the disease and the immunogenicity of ERT treatment.&nbsp;&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.38%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">AT845 has been designed to address the recognized limitations of ERT by facilitating the intracellular production of GAA directly in the tissues affected by the disease to improve efficacy, reduce immunogenicity, and deliver a durable and transformative clinical benefit from a single intravenous administration.&nbsp;&nbsp;AT845 utilizes an AAV8 capsid serotype to transfect and express GAA directly in skeletal muscle, the heart and the nervous system.&nbsp;&nbsp;This best-in-class approach stands in contrast to approved enzyme replacement therapies and liver-directed investigational gene therapy candidates that rely solely on uptake of GAA from plasma.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-right:0.64%;text-indent:5.38%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We are currently conducting preclinical dose finding and toxicology studies of AT845 to support an IND submission planned for the third quarter of 2019.</p>

AT307<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>is<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>designed<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>with the<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>goal<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>of providing<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>a single<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>administration<font style="letter-spacing:0.15pt;"> </font>that<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>results<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>in a significant<font style="letter-spacing:0.15pt;"> </font>reduction<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>in life- threatening<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>arrhythmic<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>events<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>and a major<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>improvement<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>in quality<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>of life.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-right:0.64%;text-indent:5.38%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New groups</font><font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: </font><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">development</font><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">for</font><font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">our collaborations</font><font these</font><font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">diseases</font><font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">we target and optimize</font><font research,</font><font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">development,</font><font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">and commercial</font><font normal;">plans.</font></p></td>
<td valign="top" style="width:2.56%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;color:#231F20;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-right:2.56%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Gene Therapy Background<font style="font-weight:normal;"> </font></p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.38%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Genes are composed of sequences of deoxyribonucleic acid, or DNA, which code for proteins that perform a broad range of physiologic functions within all living organisms. DNA is a large, highly charged molecule that is difficult to transport across a cell membrane and deliver to the nucleus, where it can be transcribed and translated into protein. </p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-right:2.56%;text-indent:5.38%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Gene therapy is a therapeutic approach to treating genetic diseases caused by mutations in DNA.&nbsp;&nbsp;For gene therapy to work, an isolated gene sequence or segment of DNA needs to be delivered efficiently to the desired target tissues and cell types. The treatment involves the administration of a functional gene to produce normal protein within a patient&#8217;s cells, offering the potential for durable therapeutic benefit.&nbsp;&nbsp;To achieve these goals, scientists have designed and developed a variety of viral vectors to facilitate gene delivery to cells. </p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-right:2.56%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our Approach<font style="font-weight:normal;"> </font></p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-right:2.56%;text-indent:5.38%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The AAV gene therapy vectors we utilize are capable of transducing a wide range of tissues with generally little or no toxicity and only a mild immune response.&nbsp;&nbsp;Functionally, AAV packages a single-stranded linear DNA genome that can be engineered to contain a therapeutic gene in place of all the viral genes.&nbsp;&nbsp;AAV vectors have a well-established safety profile and do not naturally propagate by themselves in the absence of another viral infection, reducing the likelihood of inappropriate viral spread following administration.&nbsp;&nbsp;As a result, AAV vectors are emerging as one of the preferred delivery vehicles for gene therapy. </p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-right:2.56%;text-indent:5.38%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our vector design strategy includes careful selection of the vector capsid (the outer protein shell) and sophisticated engineering of the vector genome (the therapeutic DNA expression cassette) to target the correct tissues and improve the potential to provide patients with meaningful and durable outcomes.&nbsp;&nbsp;Optimal selection of capsids can reduce immune responses that attenuate the function of AAV vectors, and enable more robust trafficking to the specific tissues we care about for each disease. The vector genome is composed of multiple structural elements, including the gene coding sequence and the promoter, which drives expression of the gene.&nbsp;&nbsp;We use the latest available technology to engineer the vector genome to direct the target cells to make the desired protein at the appropriate level necessary to achieve a therapeutic effect for the longest period possible.&nbsp;&nbsp;We believe the product candidates we have created offer distinct advantages for our indications due to their selectivity for target tissue types and focused expression of the desired protein.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-right:2.56%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our Product Candidate and Target Indication Selection Criteria </p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-right:2.56%;text-indent:5.38%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our business model is to develop and commercialize a broad portfolio of gene therapy product candidates to treat rare diseases. We use a focused set of criteria to select product candidates that we believe have the best chance of success. These criteria include: </p>

<td valign="top" style="width:3.85%;white-space:nowrap">

<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-right:0.43%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Our AAV Product Candidates </p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-right:0.43%;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">AT132 for the Treatment of X-Linked Myotubular Myopathy </p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-right:0.43%;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Overview of XLMTM</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-right:2.56%;text-indent:5.38%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">XLMTM is<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>characterized<font style="letter-spacing:0.15pt;"> </font>by extreme<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>muscle<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>weakness,<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>respiratory<font style="letter-spacing:0.15pt;"> </font>failure,<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>and early<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>death.&nbsp;&nbsp;Mortality<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>rates<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>are<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>estimated<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>to be 50% in the<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>first<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>18 months<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>of lif<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;">e</font>, and for<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>those<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>patients<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>who survive<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>past infancy,<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>ten-year<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>survival<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>rate<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>is<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>estimated<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>to be approximately<font style="letter-spacing:0.15pt;"> </font>75%.&nbsp;&nbsp;XLMTM places<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>a substantial<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> burden of </font>care<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>on patients,<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font><font style="color:#000000;">caregivers</font><font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>and the<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>healthcare<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>system,<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>including<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>high rates<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>of healthcare<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>utilization,<font style="letter-spacing:0.15pt;"> </font>hospitalization,<font style="letter-spacing:0.15pt;"> </font>and surgical<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>intervention.<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</font>Greater<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>than<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>80% of XLMTM patients<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>require<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>ventilator<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>support<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>and the<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>majority<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>of patients<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>require<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>a gastrostomy<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>tube<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>for<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>nutritional<font style="letter-spacing:0.15pt;"> </font>support.<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</font>In most<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>patients,<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>normal<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>developmental<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>motor milestones<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>are<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>delayed<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>or never<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>achieved.<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</font>The disease<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>is<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>result<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>of mutations<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>in the<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font><font style="font-style:italic;">MTM1</font> gene that<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>affect<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>the production<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>of myotubularin,<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>an enzyme<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>required<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>for<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>normal<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>development<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>and function<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>of skeletal<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>muscle.<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</font>The incidence<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>of XLMTM is<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>estimated<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>to range<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>between<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>approximately<font style="letter-spacing:0.15pt;"> </font>one in 40,000 to one in 50,000 male<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>births.&nbsp;&nbsp;Currently,<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>only supportive<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>treatment<font style="letter-spacing:0.15pt;"> </font>options are available,<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>such as ventilator<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>use to aid breathing, wheelchair use to aid mobility, or feeding<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>tube use<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> to aid nutrition</font>.<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font></p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-right:0.43%;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;color:#231F20;letter-spacing:0.1pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">AT132 Description<font style="font-style:normal;"> </font></p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-right:2.56%;text-indent:5.38%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">AT132 is an AAV8<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>vector<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>containing<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>a functional<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>copy of the<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font><font style="font-style:italic;">MTM1</font> gene, for<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>the<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>treatment<font style="letter-spacing:0.15pt;"> </font>of XLMTM.&nbsp;&nbsp;We believe<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>AT132<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>may<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>provide<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>patients<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>with significantly<font style="letter-spacing:0.15pt;"> </font>improved<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>outcomes<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>based<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>on the<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>ability<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>of AAV8<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>to target<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font><font style="color:#000000;">skeletal</font><font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>muscle and increase myotubularin expression in affected tissues.&nbsp;&nbsp;We believe AT132 has the potential to provide long-term clinical benefits to XLMTM patients through persistent expression of the functional protein following a single intravenous administration. </p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-right:0.43%;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Preclinical Proof-of-Concept for AT132</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-right:2.56%;text-indent:5.38%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Preclinical<font style="letter-spacing:0.15pt;"> </font>study<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font><font style="color:#000000;">results</font><font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>in both canine<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>and murine<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>models<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>of XLMTM demonstrated<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>dramatic<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> dose-dependent </font>improvements<font style="letter-spacing:0.15pt;"> </font>in all<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>outcomes,<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>including<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>histology,<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>muscle<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>strength,<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>respiratory<font style="letter-spacing:0.15pt;"> </font>function, and survival.&nbsp;&nbsp;Both models present with disease symptoms similar to that of humans, including severe muscle weakness, respiratory failure, and early death.&nbsp;&nbsp;We believe that in this indication, the canine model is particularly valuable given similarities to humans with XLMTM in terms of size, weight, and pathophysiology.&nbsp;&nbsp;Our initial canine study was designed as a proof-of-concept to determine whether AT132 could improve <font style="color:#000000;">muscle strength and organ function in comparison to an XLMTM canine treated with a placebo. Administration of a single dose of AT132 (2.0 x 10</font><font style="color:#000000;font-size:8.5pt;"><sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">14</sup></font><font style="color:#000000;">&#160;vg/kg) to nine-week-old canines weighing approximately 5 kilograms resulted in maintenance of muscle strength, respiratory function and survival comparable to normal canines.&nbsp;&nbsp;Most importantly, all treated canines achieved a statistically significant improvement in survival, which extended far beyond the critical 18-week time point, when all untreated XLMTM canines could no longer ambulate. All three of the treated canines survived for the one-year duration of the study. One of the canines was subsequently euthanized for study purposes. Six years later, the remaining two canines have grown to over twenty-five kilograms, continue to thrive, and remain indistinguishable from normal dogs.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">8</a></p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-right:0.43%;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU11"></a><font style="font-style:italic;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Clinical Development of AT132</font></p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-right:2.56%;text-indent:5.38%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The clinical development of AT132 was initiated with RECENSUS, a retrospective medical chart review designed to characterize the disease course, natural history, and unmet medical need in XLMTM.&#160;&#160; In December 2017, we announced the publication of initial data from 112 boys in RECENSUS.&nbsp;&nbsp;This analysis confirmed and expanded upon the understanding of the significant disease burden of XLMTM on patients, families and the healthcare system.&#160;&#160;We are<font style="color:#000000;"> also conducting INCEPTUS, a prospective natural history run-in study.&#160;&#160;The primary objectives of INCEPTUS are to characterize the clinical condition of children with XLMTM, identify subjects for potential enrollment in ASPIRO (the Phase 1/2 clinical study of AT132 in XLMTM), and serve as a longitudinal baseline and within-patient control for ASPIRO.&#160;&#160;Preliminary data reported from INCEPTUS confirm the significant neuromuscular and respiratory deficits experienced by XLMTM patients, and provide insight into the relevance and sensitivity of assessments used in ASPIRO.</font></p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-right:2.56%;text-indent:5.38%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">ASPIRO was designed as a multicenter, multinational, open-label, ascending dose, delayed-treatment control study to evaluate the safety and preliminary efficacy of AT132 in approximately 12 XLMTM patients less than five years of age.&#160;&#160;We initiated ASPIRO<font style="color:#000000;"> in September 2017, and the latest </font><font style="color:#231F20;">ASPIRO data set (presented in October 2018) included safety and efficacy results ranging from 4 to 48 weeks for eight patients enrolled in the trial, including seven patients enrolled in Cohort 1 (1x10<sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">14</sup> vg/kg; six treated and one untreated control) and the sentinel patient in Cohort 2 (3x10<sup style="font-size:85%; vertical-align:top">14</sup> vg/kg), as well as week 24 muscle biopsy data for the first four treated patients. </font></p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:5.38%;text-indent:0%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><font style="text-decoration:underline;">Safety</font><font style="text-decoration:underline;letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font><font style="text-decoration:underline;">Assessments</font> (as of September 20, 2018) </p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:5.38%;text-indent:0%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">AT132 was generally well-tolerated with a manageable safety profile. </p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-right:2.56%;text-indent:5.38%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As of the data cut-off date, twenty possibly<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>or probably<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>treatment-related<font style="letter-spacing:0.25pt;"> </font>adverse<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>events,<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>or AEs, had been reported<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>in ASPIRO<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>since initiation<font style="letter-spacing:0.15pt;"> </font>of the<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>study,<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>four<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>of which were determined<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>to be serious adverse events, or SAEs.<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</font>All four<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>treatment-related<font style="letter-spacing:0.25pt;"> </font>SAEs<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>occurred<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>in Patient<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>3, the<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>first<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>three<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>of which were related<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>and occurred<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>seven<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>weeks <font style="color:#000000;">post</font>-dosin<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;">g</font> and included<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>elevated creatine<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>kinase<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>and troponin<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>levels<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>that<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>were determined<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>by the<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>investigator<font style="letter-spacing:0.15pt;"> </font>to be suggestive<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>of myocarditis.<font style="letter-spacing:0.15pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</font>This episode<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>occurred<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>during<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>a period<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>when the<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>patient<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>suffered<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>a gastrointestinal<font style="letter-spacing:0.2pt;"> </font>infection<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>resulting<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>in a hospitalization.<font style="letter-spacing:0.15pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</font>The event<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>was managed<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>with medical<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>treatment<font style="letter-spacing:0.15pt;"> </font>and the<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>patient<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>was clinically<font style="letter-spacing:0.15pt;"> </font>stable<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>throughout the<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>hospital<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>admission<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>with no compromise<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>of cardiac<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>function.<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</font>At 21 weeks post-dosing,<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>Patient<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>3 was hospitalized<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>for<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>monitoring<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>of atrial<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>tachycardia,<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>a condition<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>he was noted<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>to have experienced<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>prior<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>to enrollment<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>in ASPIRO,<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>and which resolved<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>with treatment.<font style="letter-spacing:0.15pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</font>Despite<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>these<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>SAEs,<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>Patient<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>3 has shown considerable<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>neuromuscular<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>and respiratory<font style="letter-spacing:0.15pt;"> </font>functional<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>efficacy<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>gains<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>and recently<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>achieved<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>ventilator independence<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>from<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>a baseline<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>of 24-hour<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>continuous<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>invasive<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>ventilatory<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>support.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-right:2.56%;text-indent:5.38%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Sixteen non-serious AEs were determined to be either possibly or probably related to treatment.&nbsp;&nbsp;Non-serious AEs were mild and clinically asymptomatic, and all have either resolved without treatment, or been managed with treatment. Non-serious AEs included hyperbilirubinemia, elevated creatine kinase and liver transaminases, abnormal liver ultrasound, proteinuria, fever, diarrhea and vomiting.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-right:2.56%;text-indent:5.38%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">There were an additional 37 AEs determined to be non-treatment related, three of which were classified as SAEs. Non-treatment<font style="letter-spacing:0.15pt;"> </font>related<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>AEs are<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>expected<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>and associated<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>with the<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>disease<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>course<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>of XLMTM.</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">9</a></p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:5.38%;text-indent:0%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU12"></a><font style="text-decoration:underline;">Efficacy</font><font style="text-decoration:underline;letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font><font style="text-decoration:underline;">Assessments</font><font style="color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"> (As of September 26, 2018) </font></p>
<p style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:5.38%;font-size:10pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">As of the data cut-off date, AT132 showed significant improvements in neuromuscular and respiratory function (as assessed via CHOP INTEND and MIP, respectively) in all treated patients, including the Cohort 2 sentinel patient.&nbsp;&nbsp;All treated patients in Cohort 1 showed significant reductions in ventilator use, and three patients had achieved ventilator independence.&nbsp;&nbsp;Week 24 muscle biopsies showed evidence of highly efficient tissue transduction as indicated by vector copy number and robust myotubularin protein expression as assessed by Western blot.&nbsp;&nbsp;Histological analyses also show significant improvements in myofiber size, nuclear peripheralization and organelle localization<font style="color:#000000;">.</font></p>
<p style="Background-color:#FFFFFF;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="text-align:center;Background-color:#FFFFFF;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:12pt;text-indent:0%;font-size:12pt;font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><img src="gg0d5mct2jc0000002.jpg" title="" alt="" style="width:624px;height:346px;"></p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-right:1.07%;text-indent:5.38%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In addition<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>to the<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>functional<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>and histological<font style="letter-spacing:0.15pt;"> </font>improvements<font style="letter-spacing:0.15pt;"> </font>seen<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>in treated<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>patients,<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>physicians<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>and caregivers<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>have reported<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>progressive<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>qualitative<font style="letter-spacing:0.15pt;"> </font>improvements<font style="letter-spacing:0.15pt;"> </font>in disease<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>severit<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;">y</font>; improvements<font style="letter-spacing:0.15pt;"> </font>in airway clearance<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>control,<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>including<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>swallowing<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>and coughing; increased<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>limb<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>and trunk<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>strengt<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;">h</font>; and increased<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>velocity and accuracy<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>of movements.<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;">&nbsp;&nbsp;</font>Caregivers<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>also<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>report<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>that<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>patients<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>have increased<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>vocalization,<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>improving<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>their ability<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>to communicate,<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>and ability<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>to eat<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>solids<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>and drink liquids.<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>Patients<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>1 and 2 are<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>able<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>to stand<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>with support.&nbsp;&nbsp;Patient<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>1 is<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>crawlin<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;">g</font>, and Patient<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>2 is<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>initiating<font style="letter-spacing:0.15pt;"> </font>a gait<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>training<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>program. </p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-right:2.56%;text-indent:5.38%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Subsequent to the October 2018 data set, we completed initial enrollment of Cohort 2, and announced plans to further expand Cohort 2 with an additional three to five patients.&nbsp;&nbsp; </p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Regulatory Interactions and Program Next Steps</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.38%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_Hlk532242846"></a>In the fourth quarter of 2018, we completed productive initial interactions with the FDA, under the RMAT designation, and EMA, under the PRIME designation, to discuss development plans and the potential registration pathways for AT132.&nbsp;&nbsp;Feedback from the agencies was largely aligned, and we agreed that selection of the optimal dose is a key next step in the development of AT132.&nbsp;&nbsp;<font style="color:#000000;">Optimal dose selection is expected to occur in the second quarter of 2019 after the evaluation of the six-month biopsy results from the first three patients dosed in Cohort 2 of ASPIRO.&nbsp;&nbsp;Subsequent to the determination of the optimal dose, we plan to provide updated data packages to the FDA and EMA to facilitate final agreement on license registration pathways.&nbsp;&nbsp;We also received preliminary feedback on our Chemistry Manufacturing and Controls, or CMC, characterization and validation plans and plan to submit the requested information to the respective trial applications on a continuing basis.</font></p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">10</a></p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.38%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU13"></a><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We have also initiated early commercialization and BLA readiness activities, including validation efforts at our in-house cGMP manufacturing facility.</font></p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.38%;color:#231F20;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We hold exclusive<font style="letter-spacing:0.1pt;"> </font>global<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>rights<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>to both AAV8<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>and AAV9<font style="letter-spacing:-0.05pt;"> </font>in XLMTM from<font style="letter-spacing:0.05pt;"> </font>REGENXBIO, and<font style="color:#000000;"> AT132 has been granted RMAT, Rare Pediatric Disease, Fast Track and Orphan Drug designations by the FDA, and PRIME and Orphan Drug designations by the EMA.</font></p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-right:1.07%;text-indent:5.38%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The ASPIRO clinical trial is ongoing, and we plan to provide the next interim update on safety, efficacy, and muscle biopsy results at the American Society of Gene &amp; Cell Therapy 22nd Annual Meeting in 2019. </p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">AT845 for the Treatment of Pompe Disease </p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Overview of Pompe Disease </p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.38%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Pompe disease is a rare, severe, progressive, congenital neuromuscular disease. The overall incidence is estimated to be approximately one in 40,000 births, although frequency and disease progression varies with age of onset, ethnicity and geography. The disease is characterized by mutations in the gene that encodes the enzyme acid alpha-glucosidase, or GAA. GAA is responsible for degrading glycogen within the intracellular organelle known as the lysosome.&#160;&#160;Dysfunction or absence of functional GAA results in toxic accumulation of glycogen in the lysosome. Tissues and cells most affected by the disease are predominantly skeletal muscle, cardiac muscle and the nervous system.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.38%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The severity of Pompe disease symptoms and rate of progression is highly variable and correlated with age of symptom onset and the degree of enzyme deficiency. Infantile-onset disease, the most severe form of Pompe disease, accounts for approximately one quarter of all affected patients. Those with infantile-onset disease are usually diagnosed in the first few months of life due to the severe presentation associated with total or near- total absence of GAA activity, and confirmatory diagnosis is made through genetic testing. These infants usually present with feeding difficulties, failure to thrive, hypotonia, progressive weakness, respiratory distress, severe enlargement of the tongue and thickening of the heart muscle. If left untreated, these children usually die in the first year of life. Those with late-onset disease typically have enzyme levels at 1% to 40% of normal and usually have symptoms such as reduced mobility and respiratory problems. Late-onset patients experience progressive difficulty walking and respiratory decline, and although life expectancy can vary, it is a life-limiting disease and death generally occurs due to complications from respiratory failure. Newborn screening programs can successfully identify Pompe disease in the newborn period, but such programs have not yet been widely implemented worldwide.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Limitations of Current Therapy for Pompe Disease</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:6.58%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The only approved treatment for Pompe disease is enzyme replacement therapy, or ERT, which is a chronic treatment delivered in bi-weekly intravenous infusions.&nbsp;&nbsp;Despite the availability of ERT, significant medical need persists, which is primarily due to the immunogenicity of ERT and its inability to penetrate key tissues affected by the disease.&nbsp;&nbsp;Although ERT is the current standard of care for Pompe disease, it has a number of recognized limitations:</p>
<div align="left">
<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0"  style="border-collapse:collapse; width:100%;">

<td valign="top" style="width:5.38%;white-space:nowrap">

<td valign="top" style="width:3.85%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#x2022;</font></p></td>
<td valign="top">
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;color:#000000;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;">Currently approved versions of ERT are administered every two weeks, and in some cases more frequently.</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
<div align="left">

<td valign="top" style="width:3.85%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#x2022;</font></p></td>
<td valign="top">
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;color:#000000;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;">Large doses of ERT have to be delivered systemically in order to achieve potentially therapeutic levels in target tissues, and as a result approximately 90% of patients develop antibodies against the therapy.  Such antibody responses may impact both the safety and efficacy of ERT.  Currently approved ERT products carry a black box warning related to the risk of life-threatening anaphylaxis, and severe allergic and immune mediated reactions.</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
<div align="left">
<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0"  style="border-collapse:collapse; width:100%;">

<td valign="top" style="width:3.85%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#x2022;</font></p></td>

<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;color:#000000;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;">While initial studies of ERT demonstrated that treatment improved survival and ventilator-free survival of patients with early-onset disease, long-term follow-up of these patients indicates substantial disease progression.  Subsequent analyses of the effectiveness of ERT have identified variations in outcomes, with most infants exhibiting declines in motor and respiratory function and reduced survival despite treatment.</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">11</a></p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>

<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#x2022;</font></p></td>
<td valign="top">
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;color:#000000;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU14"></a><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"></font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"></font><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;">ERT is unable to cross the blood-brain barrier and thus cannot reduce the accumulation of glycogen in the nervous system. </font><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;"> </font><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;">It is believed that glycogen accumulation is particularly detrimental to the function of the neural cells, and thus the inability of ERT to reach these cells may lead to incomplete treatment of the underlying pathology and account for the failure of ERT to halt disease progression and reverse functional decline</font><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;">.</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
<div align="left">
<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0"  style="border-collapse:collapse; width:100%;">
<tr>
<td valign="top" style="width:5.38%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;color:#000000;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p></td>
<td valign="top" style="width:3.85%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#x2022;</font></p></td>
<td valign="top">
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;color:#000000;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;">Chronic therapy with ERT is costly.  Experts in health technology assessment have projected the lifetime costs of ERT to be in excess of $7 million for patients with infantile onset Pompe.  Due to the requirement of dosing by body weight, the cost for infantile patients increases year-over-year as these patients grow.</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">AT845 Description </p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.38%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">AT845 has been designed to address the recognized limitations of ERT by facilitating the intracellular production of GAA to improve efficacy, reduce immunogenicity, and deliver a durable and transformative clinical benefit from a single intravenous administration.&nbsp;&nbsp;AT845 utilizes an AAV8 capsid serotype to transfect and express GAA directly in tissues affected by the disease, including skeletal muscle, the heart and the nervous system.&nbsp;&nbsp;This best-in-class approach stands in contrast to approved enzyme replacement therapies and liver-directed investigational gene therapy candidates that rely solely on uptake of GAA from plasma.&nbsp;&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Planned Development of AT845</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.38%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In early 2018 we presented robust proof-of-concept data confirming the ability of systemically administered AAV gene therapy to transfect and express GAA in tissues affected by Pompe disease.&nbsp;&nbsp;These data were generated in the Pompe mouse model with a prototype version of AT845 and demonstrated improved muscle pathology; GAA expression and activity in skeletal and cardiac muscle, and the nervous system; and a favorable immunogenicity profile<font style="color:#000000;">.</font></p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.38%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">We are currently conducting preclinical dose finding and toxicology studies of AT845 to support an IND submission planned for the third quarter of 2019.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Regulatory Interactions</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.38%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Both the FDA and EMA have granted Orphan Drug designation to a prototype version of AT845, which we plan to update to reflect our new construct.&nbsp;&nbsp;We hold exclusive global rights to both AAV8 and AAV9 in Pompe disease from REGENXBIO.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">AT342 for the Treatment of Crigler-Najjar</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Overview of Crigler-Najjar</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:6.58%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Crigler-Najjar is a rare, congenital autosomal recessive monogenic disease characterized by severely high levels of bilirubin in the blood and risk of irreversible neurological damage and death. Crigler-Najjar is caused by mutations in the gene encoding the UGT1A1 (uridine-diphosphate (UDP)-glucuronosyltransferase (UGT) 1A1) enzyme resulting in an inability to convert unconjugated bilirubin to a water-soluble form that can be excreted from the body. Unconjugated bilirubin can cross the blood brain barrier, and the accumulation of unconjugated bilirubin in the central nervous system can lead to irreversible neurological damage and death.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.38%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Infants with Crigler-Najjar develop severe jaundice shortly after birth resulting in rapid presentation and diagnosis. Clinical diagnosis can be confirmed via genetic testing of the UGT1A1 gene. The current standard of care for Crigler-Najjar is aggressive management of high bilirubin levels with persistent, daily phototherapy, usually for longer than 10 to 12 hours per day, for the rest of a patient&#8217;s life. Exchange transfusion or plasmapheresis are sometimes required in order to lower bilirubin levels rapidly. Phototherapy becomes less effective as a child ages, beginning around the age of four years. Average life expectancy is reported as being 30 years of age with phototherapy, and there is an ongoing lifelong risk of a catastrophic cerebral event. Crigler-Najjar is estimated to affect approximately one in 1,000,000 newborns.</p>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">12</a></p>
<hr style="page-break-after:always;width:100%;">
<p style="margin-bottom:0pt;margin-top:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><a name="_AEIOULastRenderedPageBreakAEIOU15"></a><font style="font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Limitations of Current Therapy for Crigler-Najjar</font></p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.38%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">There are currently no products approved specifically for the treatment of Crigler-Najjar. The current standard of care for Crigler-Najjar is aggressive management of high bilirubin levels, with persistent, daily phototherapy, usually for longer than 10 to 12 hours per day using intense fluorescent light focused on the bare skin, while the eyes are shielded. Phototherapy speeds bilirubin decomposition and excretion, lowering serum bilirubin to levels that are just below those considered to be neurotoxic. The impact on quality of life is substantial. As children get older, compliance with phototherapy becomes challenging. As Crigler-Najjar infants and children begin to experience progression of neurological symptoms and increasing risk of a catastrophic cerebral event, a liver transplant is often required for survival. However, limited donor organ availability, the risks associated with the transplant procedure itself and potential for organ rejection limit the utility of a transplant as a treatment modality for Crigler-Najjar.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">AT342 Description</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.38%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">AT342 consists of an AAV8 vector capsid designed to deliver a functional UGT1A1 gene and express the UGT1A1 protein in the liver. Importantly, AAV8 has high affinity for liver cells allowing for the efficient introduction of therapeutic genes into liver cells. We believe that AT342 has the potential to provide long-term clinical benefit to Crigler-Najjar patients through persistent expression of the protein following a single administration, resulting in significant reduction in bilirubin levels, reduction or elimination of the need for lengthy daily phototherapy treatment and elimination of the need for a liver transplant.</p>
<p style="margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-style:italic;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">Clinical Development of AT342</p>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:5.38%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">The clinical development plan for AT342 consists of LUSTRO, a clinical assessment and Phase 1/2 run-in study designed to characterize the disease course, natural history, bilirubin variability and phototherapy usage of patients with Crigler-Najjar and VALENS, the Phase 1/2 clinical study of AT342.</p>

<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;color:#000000;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p></td>
<td valign="top" style="width:3.85%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#x2022;</font></p></td>
<td valign="top">
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;color:#000000;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;">LUSTRO - Clinical Assessment and Phase 1/2 Run-in Study:</font><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;"> LUSTRO is an international, clinical assessment study of approximately five to ten patients greater than or equal to one year of age with Crigler-Najjar. The primary objective of this study is to characterize the disease course, natural history, bilirubin variability and phototherapy usage of patients with Crigler-Najjar, with a specific focus on serum bilirubin levels and time on phototherapy. In addition, the study will assess the burden of disease on Crigler-Najjar subjects and caregivers. The study is also expected to identify patients for potential enrollment in VALENS, the Phase 1/2 study of Crigler-Najjar, and to serve as a within-patient control for VALENS.</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;margin-left:9.23%;text-indent:0%;color:#000000;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">In October 2017, we presented a preliminary analysis from three patients enrolled in LUSTRO.&#160;&#160;These data confirm that despite persistent daily phototherapy, total bilirubin levels in Crigler Najjar patients are maintained only just below levels that are known to be neurotoxic.&#160;&#160;These data further confirm the significant burden of disease for patients and caregivers and the ongoing risk of catastrophic cerebral events associated with phototherapy.</p>

<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;color:#000000;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;">&nbsp;</p></td>
<td valign="top" style="width:3.85%;white-space:nowrap">
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">&#x2022;</font></p></td>
<td valign="top">
<p style="margin-top:6pt;margin-bottom:0pt;color:#000000;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;"><font style="font-style:italic;font-family:Times New Roman;">VALENS - Phase 1/2 Study:</font><font style="font-family:Times New Roman;"> The Phase 1/2 study of AT342 is a multicenter, multinational, open-label, ascending dose, delayed-treatment concurrent control study to evaluate the safety and preliminary efficacy of AT342 in approximately 12 Crigler-Najjar patients greater than or equal to one year of age. The study was designed to include nine AT342 treated subjects and three delayed-treatment concurrent control subjects.&#160;&#160;Primary endpoints include safety (adverse events and certain laboratory measures, including immunological parameters) and efficacy (changes in serum bilirubin and number of hours on phototherapy).&#160; Secondary endpoints include the proportion of subjects successfully weaned off of phototherapy, and UGT1A1 protein expression, DNA and RNA levels from liver biopsy at 24 weeks. Subjects are expected to remain on prescribed phototherapy for 12 weeks following administration of AT342.&#160;&#160;Subjects with a meaningful decrease in bilirubin at week 12 will be tapered down and weaned off of phototherapy over a five-week period, starting in week 13 and ending during week 17.&#160;&#160;The primary efficacy analyses are conducted at the 12 and 18-week time points.</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
<p style="text-align:center;margin-top:12pt;margin-top:12pt;margin-bottom:0pt;text-indent:0%;font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10pt;font-weight:normal;font-style:normal;text-transform:none;font-variant: normal;">13</a></p>
